content: Does useReducer work well with TypeScript?

replies.content: Excellent with TypeScript, useReducer is! Discriminated unions, use you should.

content: What about useReducer with Redux Toolkit's createSlice? Can they work together?

replies.content: They solve similar problems! createSlice is essentially useReducer on steroids for global state. Pick one approach - don't mix them.

content: Will the late penalty still apply after original deadline?

replies.content: No late penalty before new deadline. After December 10th, standard late policy applies.

content: What about Zustand? Simpler than Redux but more powerful than Context?

replies.content: Used Zustand - highly recommend! Simple API, no boilerplate.
Zustand is excellent for the project. Document your choice in the report!

content: I'm getting infinite redirects even with stable auth state. Using useContext for auth. Any ideas?

replies.content: Check if your Navigate component is inside the auth provider. The context value might not be ready on first render.
That was it! Added a loading state while auth initializes. Works perfectly now!

content: Should custom hooks always start with 'use'? What if I forget?

replies.content: Start with 'use', they must! Rules of Hooks, ESLint enforces. Without 'use', work it will not.

content: Gradient clipping worked! But now underfitting. Increase LR again?

replies.content: Try learning rate scheduler - start high and decay.
Cosine annealing or ReduceLROnPlateau are good options.

content: Oh my! What about data augmentation? Should I implement it myself or use a library?

replies.content: Use torchvision.transforms! It has random rotations, flips, color jitter, and more. No need to reinvent the wheel.

content: Is there a visualization tool for recursion trees?

replies.content: Python Tutor is great! Also check out Recursion Tree Visualizer on GitHub.
Will add links to lecture notes. Great suggestion!

content: What about bidirectional BFS? When is that better than regular BFS?

replies.content: Bidirectional BFS is faster when you know both start and end points! Search from both ends until they meet. Reduces search space significantly.

content: Dude, what about BCNF? Is that different from 3NF?

replies.content: BCNF is stricter! 3NF handles most cases, but BCNF eliminates ALL anomalies from functional dependencies. For this course, focus on 3NF.

content: What about IPv6 subnetting? Is it on the exam?

replies.content: IPv6 conceptually only. Exam focuses on IPv4 calculations.

content: Goodness! Does Figma have version control like Git?

replies.content: Yeah bro! Figma auto-saves versions. You can restore old versions from the file menu. It's totally radical!

content: What if I have multiple Docker Compose files running? How do I know which one is using the port?

replies.content: Run: docker-compose ps in each project directory. Or use: docker ps to see all running containers with their ports.

content: *Beep boop?* (How do I know when NOT to optimize?)

replies.content: Premature optimization is the root of all evil! Only optimize when you have a measured performance problem. Profile first!

content: What's the file size difference between Client and Server Components?

replies.content: Server Components don't ship ANY JavaScript to the client! My bundle went from 300KB to 120KB by moving static components to server.

content: Is multi-head attention just multiple attention mechanisms in parallel?

replies.content: Exactly! Each head learns different relationships. Like having multiple advisors - one focuses on syntax, another on semantics, etc. Then concatenate their outputs.
Oh my! So it's like having multiple protocols running simultaneously! Fascinating!

content: Heavens! For the heuristic in A*, can I use Manhattan distance for a grid with obstacles?

replies.content: Yes! Manhattan distance is perfect for grid-based movement (up/down/left/right). It's admissible because it never overestimates the actual path cost.

content: What's the difference between deadlock prevention and deadlock avoidance?

replies.content: Prevention: Make deadlock impossible by breaking one of the four conditions (like requiring processes to request all resources at once). Avoidance: Allow all four conditions but intelligently decide when to grant resources (like Banker's Algorithm).

content: *Beep boop beep boop!* (What if I want variable quantum per process?)

replies.content: That's Multi-Level Feedback Queue! Different queues with different quantum sizes. Smooth idea! More complex but better for mixed workloads.

content: Cowabunga! What about telnet to test if the HTTP port is open?

replies.content: Great idea! telnet serverIP 80 will tell you if the port is open. Or use: nc -zv serverIP 80

content: Pizza time! How long should I run the A/B test? Just until significance?

replies.content: Run for at least one full week to account for day-of-week effects. And decide on sample size BEFORE starting - don't peek at results and stop early!

content: Dude, can I use Terraform modules from the community?

replies.content: Use them, you may! Terraform Registry, many good modules has. But understand what they do, you must. Blind trust, dangerous it is!

content: What about Vite instead of CRA? I heard it's much faster.

replies.content: Vite is excellent! Instant hot module replacement. CRA is being deprecated anyway. Vite or Next.js are both great choices for new projects.

content: Does React Hook Form work well with TypeScript?

replies.content: Perfectly! Type inference works great. You get autocomplete for field names and everything is type-safe.

content: Should I try ensemble methods to combat overfitting?

replies.content: Ensembling can help but fix the base model first! Make sure one model generalizes well before combining multiple models.
